# 04. UX

<!-- Generated by tools/build_checklists.py. Edit the generator to change checklist structure. -->

**Purpose:** Ensure the site helps real users complete meaningful tasks with clarity, confidence, speed, and minimal friction.

## Universal Constraints
- [ ] The solution must remain static front-end only: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, documents, and generated static files only.
- [ ] The stack must avoid proprietary lock-in, paid builders, paid plugins, closed hosting features that cannot be replaced, and opaque third-party scripts where an open or free-tier-friendly alternative exists.
- [ ] Every decision must be documented as a quality rule, acceptance criterion, or exception with rationale; implementation notes belong outside the checklist.
- [ ] Every checklist item must be testable by review, automated audit, source inspection, browser testing, or client sign-off.
- [ ] Manual exceptions must record the owner, reason, expiration date, affected pages, and residual risk.

## Must Exist
- [ ] A primary journey map for each priority audience and conversion path.
- [ ] A task model for finding services, evaluating proof, checking fit, contacting the business, reading content, or reviewing work.
- [ ] A page intent statement for every template and important standalone page.
- [ ] A CTA hierarchy defining primary, secondary, and tertiary actions by page type.
- [ ] A friction register covering confusing copy, excessive fields, hidden pricing, unclear next steps, slow pages, and trust gaps.
- [ ] A mobile UX standard covering thumb reach, tap target size, sticky elements, navigation behavior, form flow, and content order.
- [ ] A states inventory for hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, success, error, empty, offline, and reduced-motion experiences.
- [ ] A user feedback plan using free methods such as manual usability review, browser recordings only with consent, or moderated sessions.

## Must Be True
- [ ] The first viewport must communicate where the user is, what is offered, why it matters, and what action is available.
- [ ] Users must not need to understand the business internally to navigate the site.
- [ ] Primary actions must remain visible or easy to find without trapping users in sticky UI.
- [ ] Copy, layout, and interaction order must match the user's decision sequence.
- [ ] Mobile users must receive the same essential content and conversion options as desktop users.
- [ ] Interactive components must be usable by mouse, keyboard, touch, and assistive technology.
- [ ] Error states must explain the issue and recovery path without blaming the user.
- [ ] The experience must remain coherent when JavaScript fails unless the feature explicitly requires JavaScript.

## Must Be Checked
- [ ] Check that users can answer: what is this, is it for me, why trust it, what does it cost or require, and what happens next.
- [ ] Check that each page has a clear next step without forcing premature contact.
- [ ] Check that contact details, service areas, hours, credentials, and constraints are visible where decision anxiety occurs.
- [ ] Check that modals, drawers, accordions, tabs, menus, and carousels are accessible and not required for critical information.
- [ ] Check that forms preserve user input on validation errors wherever static architecture allows.
- [ ] Check that animations do not block interaction, obscure content, or violate reduced-motion preferences.
- [ ] Check that page layouts work at small mobile, large mobile, tablet, laptop, desktop, and zoomed text sizes.
- [ ] Check that users can identify visited, focused, disabled, selected, and current states.

## Must Be Avoided
- [ ] Avoid hero sections that delay useful content with vague slogans.
- [ ] Avoid hiding essential information behind sliders, hover-only interactions, or decorative reveals.
- [ ] Avoid forced newsletter popups, intrusive chat widgets, and sticky banners that compete with conversion tasks.
- [ ] Avoid infinite scroll for content users may need to revisit, share, or search.
- [ ] Avoid form friction that asks for information before explaining why it is needed.
- [ ] Avoid dark patterns, fake urgency, confirm-shaming, or preselected consent.

## Premium Acceptance Standard
- [ ] The site must feel calm, fast, predictable, and complete under real browsing conditions.
- [ ] Every interaction must have an obvious affordance, feedback state, and escape path.
- [ ] The UX must support scanning first, then deeper evaluation.
- [ ] Premium UX must be measured by decision confidence and task completion, not by novelty.

## Automation Hooks
- [ ] Use audits to flag tiny tap targets indirectly through CSS review, missing labels, broken links, keyboard traps requiring manual review, and JavaScript-dependent navigation.
- [ ] Use manual QA scripts for journeys that cannot be validated from source alone.

## Detailed Best-Practice Review Areas
- [ ] Purpose and strategy UX: users understand what the business does, who it serves, why it differs, and what to do next within seconds.
- [ ] Page narrative: each page has a logical beginning, middle, proof, and final CTA; sections flow from broad to specific, problem to solution, proof to action.
- [ ] Header, footer, hero, content, CTA, form, trust, media, legal, analytics, error, empty, and final QA experiences are reviewed as part of the user journey.
- [ ] Mobile UX is intentionally designed: readable text, large tap targets, natural stacking, no horizontal scroll, usable menu, accessible contact actions, and no sticky element blocking content.
- [ ] Interaction UX includes click/tap affordance, hover/focus/active/disabled states, purposeful motion, reduced-motion support, smooth menus, predictable accordions/tabs, and recoverable cookie banners.
- [ ] Trust and credibility appear before high-friction actions through specific proof, contact information, transparency, legal/privacy access, and no fake urgency or unsupported hype.
- [ ] The ultimate UX rule is enforced: clear, structured, persuasive, fast, polished, maintainable, and complete enough to behave like a real business system.

## Report Output Required
- [ ] Report every failed automated check with severity, checklist category, issue code, affected file or page, evidence, whether it is script-fixable, and how to fix it.
- [ ] Report every manual-only failure with reviewer, affected page or component, expected standard, actual behavior, recommended fix, owner, and target date.
- [ ] Separate launch blockers from quality improvements so critical static-site failures cannot be hidden by low-priority polish notes.
- [ ] Attach the JSON audit report, Markdown audit report, screenshots where visual proof is needed, and manual QA evidence for browser, device, keyboard, screen reader, form, analytics, and live deployment checks.

## Evidence Required
- [ ] Record reviewed pages, tools used, dates, reviewers, unresolved exceptions, and links to generated reports.
- [ ] Attach screenshots or source references for failures that cannot be proven by automated reports.
- [ ] Mark checklist items as complete only when the production static output satisfies the rule.
